items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Well, yes, he was a mainstay in my band for years. I got Mickey. We call him Mickey. Mickey Alcorn. I brought him out of New Orleans when he was a kid, too.

ctx.x: Anything, let's see, Alvin Alcorn, of course, was over here for a while, I understand, and played with you. He was interviewed for Tulane, too, but I've never heard his interview. Another fellow up there, Dick Allen, interviewed him.

Well, yes, he was a mainstay in my band for years. I got Mickey. We call him Mickey. Mickey Alcorn. I brought him out of New Orleans when he was a kid, too. I never heard him call that Mickey. Mickey. I never heard him. Just when you see him, say, hi, Mickey. Yeah. I never heard anybody call him that over there.
He still plays the parade. Oh, he's fine.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: We had the James sisters and Mickey and I would do a little scene.

ctx.x: When you were working on the percentage, you would watch the game.

Well, now there you go again. A lot of times they asked me why did I stop playing like I did. Well, for more reasons than one. That was one of them to stay on the door and watch the proceedings there and make sure that I got everything was mine. That's what happened when we were on the verge of being lynched in Thomasville, Georgia, playing a percentage dance and the school teacher had charge of the dance. And naturally I was up there checking the door with him when the policemen came in to arrest everybody,…

We have talked about it some, but I didn't get everything down, you know. Oh, we didn't? Yeah. Like that, you know, and every time you tell something you get more. Did you ever know a fella named Floyd Snellson?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Alcorn and I had an act together on that.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, we talked about that, Billy. How about, say, what sort of acts did the guys in the band have? Did they have anything like Lunsford with all the folks? And Lunsford with all the throwing of the instruments in the air. Did you ever do anything like that?

Yeah. Well, Alcorn and I had an act together on that. We had this act together. I'd have Alcorn sit on my lap. He was such a young captain. He was small. And we'd blow the horn. I'd cross. I'd blow. I'd finger his horn. He'd finger mine. A little trick that we thought of meant on there. And we'd throw the instruments in there. And there's some finale. And in those days, standing in the chairs sometime or doing something just to create attention from the audience while you had to do it.
Oh, yeah. They expected you to. They expected you to do that. Did you wave the instruments around ever, doing anything like that? Do which?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-29
items.q: In this band? Yeah. Alvin Alcorn.

ctx.x: In this band? Yeah. Alvin Alcorn. Always? Well, until after I stopped. I was in the same room. Then at one time, there was a little fella named Sean Anderson, but he didn't last at all. He copied Billy Douglas' style.
